gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much of the headline split-phase rating you can draw on one 120 V leg. EG4's 6000XP manual caps output current at 25 A, which works out to about 3,000 W on a single 120 V leg, half its 6 kW label. EG4's 18kPV manual says that unit can take up to 8 kW of imbalance between L1 and L2.
standout_why: I read four of the pages ChatGPT got. Eco Solar Kits 'EG4 vs Sol-Ark 2026' (cited) gives battery-only vs with-solar output and surge durations of 0.5 s, 10 s and 10 min, and it already warns that surge numbers can't be compared directly. So surge is covered. It says nothing about 120 V per-leg output, imbalance or idle draw. NAZ Solar Electric's buying guide (cited) gives battery-only vs grid output and 10 s / 0.5 s surge but has no per-leg or idle figures. Solar Gear Scout's 'Off-Grid vs Hybrid' guide (cited) says surge lasts anywhere from 0.5 s to 300 s but gives no per-leg limits. I could not open gearranking.com (cited) because of an SSL certificate error, so I can't say whether it covers this. Every page I read lists one total wattage at 240 V and never says how much of it a 120 V-heavy home can use.
decides: This matters most for ChatGPT's 'best budget off-grid' pick. If a cabin or shop runs mostly 120 V loads, the EG4 6000XP behaves like a 3 kW inverter per leg, not 6 kW, so the shopper may need two units or a different inverter. The EG4 18kPV handles up to 8 kW of imbalance, which supports keeping it as the value pick for whole-home backup where loads are rarely balanced. I couldn't open a source for the Sol-Ark 15K's per-leg rating, so the comparison table has to footnote it as missing rather than fill it in.
candidates: Sun Gold Power 6000W 48V Split Phase Inverter Charger

findings.label: L1/L2 load imbalance it can carry
findings.note: Manual p.33, split-phase service section: 'The inverter can withstand up to 8kW of imbalance between L1 and L2.' The same section advises keeping loads as balanced as possible.

findings.label: Idle consumption, normal vs standby
findings.note: Manual p.6 spec table: 'IDLE CONSUMPTION (NORMAL | STANDBY MODE) ~70W | ~18W'. At 70 W the unit uses about 1.7 kWh a day.

findings.label: Rated AC output
findings.note: The maker's page gives only 'AC Output: 12kW continuous' and does not split on-grid from battery output.

findings.label: Price
findings.note: Signature Solar is EG4's US store. The page shows $4,898.00 struck through. ChatGPT also showed $3,999.99, at PowerGen Store.

findings.label: Max continuous AC output current
findings.note: The manual's FAQ says '25A at 240V' and points to p.5. The p.5 output table was cut off in the copy I read. 25 A × 240 V = 6,000 W, which matches the rating. Each leg conductor carries the same 25 A, so a load on only one 120 V leg tops out at 25 A × 120 V = 3,000 W. That per-leg figure is my arithmetic, not the manual's wording.

findings.label: Per-leg 120 V limit, surge and idle (named third party)
findings.value: 3,000 W per 120 V leg; surge 12 kW for 3.5 s / 11 kW for 5 s; idle 50 W on battery, 30 W on PV only
findings.note: SolarTech says 'Per-leg limitation: 3000W maximum per 120V leg' and that 4,000 W on one leg overloads the inverter. That matches the 25 A arithmetic above. SolarTech cites a source only for the idle figure (Signature Solar and ShopSolar, no link).

findings.label: Max continuous AC output and price
findings.source_title: Sol-Ark 15K-2P Limitless Pre-wired Hybrid Inverter System (NAZ Solar Electric)
findings.note: NAZ's product page has no per-leg, battery-only, surge or idle figures. Its buying guide (a cited rival) gives 12 kW battery-only and 24 kVA for 10 s off-grid surge.

findings.label: Surge figures quoted by rivals over different time windows
findings.value: 0.5 s (EG4 12kPV, FlexBOSS18), 10 s (Sol-Ark 12K/15K/18K), 10 min (EG4 18kPV: 13.5 kW without PV, 14.7 kW with PV)
findings.source_title: EG4 vs Sol-Ark 2026: Hybrid Inverters Compared (Eco Solar Kits)
findings.note: This rival page already has the surge-duration point, so it isn't new. It gives the 6000XP's 12 kW surge with no duration.
